frontier.hypothesis: The `sw s5,44(sp) / move s5,a0` block-0 group can be rotated from position 1 to position 3, which would take the sanctioned do-while(0) carrier from 4 to 0 and make the function submittable under the do-while-zero family.
frontier.mechanism: sched2 orders the three (save, init) groups by the ascending INSN_LUID tie-break; the parameter copy `move s5,a0` has the lowest LUID because expand_function_start emits it before the body, while the target's RTL has it after `select = 0` and `special = 0`. tools/sched_solver confirms the goal order is reachable by moving the statement that owns LUID 4 to just before LUID 21 or 23.
frontier.next_probe: Resolve the uid->source-statement mapping the solver is talking about, then spell the vector. goalmap.py has no --target-object flag, so read the mapping either from the model JSON (tmp/sched_solver_work/ings.sched.json - decode its block/insn schema; it was NOT decoded this session) or from a `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80016E60` .sched2 dump, matching uids 4, 21, 23 to their RTL patterns. Recipe: apply memory/grind/func_80016E60/carrier_u8shift_dowhile_4.c, run the sandbox, then extract.py ings -> mkasm.sh ings -> perturb.py --pass 2 --target-object build/src/ings.o --ours-object tmp/sandbox/func_80016E60/ings.o. Five hand permutations are already banked as dead (rejected/*prologue-worse*, swap-select-special-init-4-but-12-lines.c), so do not re-sweep by hand.

frontier.hypothesis: The QImode mechanism behind the u8-shift win is birthing_insn_p's `GET_CODE (SET_DEST (pat)) == REG` guard failing on a narrow destination, not a change in reg_n_sets - and if so the same guard is a general, reusable lever for every sched1 birthing-boost residual in the project.
frontier.mechanism: tools/gcc-2.7.2/sched.c:2504 gates the adjust_priority boost on a conjunction; three sessions attacked reg_n_sets and were defeated by cse2, while the dest-form conjunct had never been probed. s16 and u32 measured inert (15), which is consistent with QImode being the only spelling that changes the dest form here.
frontier.next_probe: Run the instrumented cc1 (tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1, BB2_SCHED_DEBUG=1 BB2_PRIO_DEBUG=1) on the u8-shift body and grep the ADJPRI lines for the arm's addiu: a `birth=0` on an insn whose reg still has reg_n_sets == 1 confirms the dest-form attribution; a `birth=1` that simply never wins would mean the mechanism is something else (e.g. a changed LUID layout from an extra extend insn that combine later folds). Record the verdict either way - the answer generalises beyond this function.

frontier.hypothesis: An HONEST env/select seat lever still exists and would leave the function needing only the block-0 fix, with no FAKE construct at all.
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocno_compare: env has 3 byte-visible refs x loop_depth 2 = 6 weighted, pri 4615 at livelen 26; select is 27/157 = 6878. env wins at 8 weighted refs or livelen <= 17 (killed by s2 E-s2-2), or if select drops to <= 16 weighted refs (~6.5 in-loop refs against the present 12) or its livelen stretches past ~234. The only honest lever measured so far is split-init accumulation on env (s2 H6), which took the seat but cost 3 points on the OLD arm shape.
frontier.next_probe: Re-measure the s2 H6 honest split-init env form (`env = (u8 *)(idx * 0x4090); env += (s32)&D_800F7438;`) ON TOP OF the new u8-shift arm shape - it has never been composed with it, and its two costs (one operand parked in env's own hard reg, plus three lost reorg.c back-edge peels of `li a1,1`) may interact differently now that the arms move no instructions. Also sweep select's in-loop reference count: the two ?: arms each read `select` twice, so a spelling that reads it once per arm is the only untried route to the <=16 weighted refs the arithmetic needs.
